## Context

Today `rebar bridge` exposes `{preview,sync,pause,resume}`. No `bridge status` subcommand exists, and the earlier top-level `bridge-status` command was fully removed. This story creates canonical `rebar bridge status` over durable state and re-introduces `rebar bridge-status` as a compatibility alias. Both spellings use the same parser and core so options, text and JSON schemas, messages, state reads, and exit codes stay identical. Existing preview, sync, pause, and resume behavior remains unchanged.

The current production canary queries GitHub Actions for heartbeat state. Reconciler health also has two overlapping producers: `health.record_pass` and `pass_io._write_pass_record`. The per-pass `bridge_state/health/<pass_id>.json` files live in an ignored ephemeral directory and are not durable. The tickets branch is durable, but the workflow commit-back step at lines 309-310 is gated by `if: steps.reconcile.outputs.paused != true` and is skipped after a reconcile step exits nonzero because it lacks `always()`. Therefore commit-back cannot witness a hard failure.

## Durable state and writer contract

Consolidate the two pass-record producers into one. A mutating reconciler pass writes minimal JSON truth to the Git object named by `refs/reconciler/last-pass` from process-level finalization that runs for both success and process-surviving hard failure. The record contains schema version, pass id, selected environment id, outcome, failure kind when present, completion timestamp, and the lock fence observed for the pass. The ref is authoritative.

Update the ref with observed-OID compare-and-swap using `--force-with-lease=refs/reconciler/last-pass:<observed-oid>`. Reuse the existing CAS and mismatch-classification seams in `_ref_lock.py` and `_advisory_lock.py`; do not introduce a second mismatch classifier. Make at most three total attempts, refetching after each CAS mismatch and sleeping 100 ms then 200 ms before retries. Exhausted contention or persistent push, network, or permission failure is an operational failure: emit a clear error, force a nonzero reconciler result, and never claim that the pass was durably recorded.

Finalization advances `refs/reconciler/last-pass` before releasing `refs/reconciler/lock`. Keep the lock heartbeat active through the last-pass CAS, then stop heartbeat and release promptly after the CAS finishes, avoiding a long non-advancing finalization window. While CAS retries, the lock remains held and status reports `RUNNING`. The fence copied into last-pass is provenance only; every `RUNNING` or canary `CRASHED` decision uses the live lock-ref snapshot and never the recorded fence. After a successful ref advance the lock is released. If all ref writes fail, finalization still releases the lock to avoid a false crash witness but preserves the nonzero operational failure, leaving the prior authoritative record visibly stale rather than inventing success.

Rich detail is one fixed rolling file, `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/last-pass.json`, overwritten rather than accumulated per pass and committed through the normal tickets-branch path when that path runs. Status uses detail only when pass id and environment id match the authoritative ref record. Missing, stale, or mismatched rich detail is reported as `detail_status` and omitted from the detail payload; it never replaces or changes the authoritative verdict.

Remove duplicate producers plus dead `pre_fsck`, `post_fsck`, and `capture_baseline` data. Update every caller and assertion in `health.py`, `pass_io.py`, `reconcile.py`, `applier.py`, health/schema/baseline/wiring tests, invariant/filter tests, store compatibility, and scratch-exclusion tests. After claim, perform semantic reference lookup plus an `rg` string and monkeypatch sweep before removal, then repeat the sweep after implementation to prove `_write_pass_record`, the old `record_pass`, `capture_baseline`, `pre_fsck`, and `post_fsck` have no live references.

## Environment identity

This identity rule is scoped only to the new last-pass writer and status target; it does not modify inbound event metadata. An explicit `REBAR_ENV_ID` always wins. The reconcile workflow continues explicitly supplying `${{ vars.REBAR_ENV_ID || reconciler }}`, preserving current CI behavior. Outside that workflow, an unset last-pass writer id becomes stable `local:<repo-env-id>` from the checkout `.env-id`; that new writer must not implicitly select `reconciler`. Preserve `inbound_translate._event_meta`, `LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID=reconciler`, and the reducer legacy-Jira inference unchanged. Status accepts an explicit target environment option. When that option is omitted, it uses the same identity selection as the last-pass writer: explicit `REBAR_ENV_ID` wins, otherwise a local checkout selects stable `local:<repo-env-id>` from `.env-id`. A missing, empty, or unreadable `.env-id` is a hard configuration error for both writer and status; it never falls back to `reconciler` or an empty/unknown identity. The canary explicitly requests `reconciler`, so a developer last-pass record is healthy to its local default target but `FOREIGN` to the production target, without breaking existing event vocabulary or projection.

## Status snapshot and exact contract

`bridge status` is a fast, read-only, non-mutating single snapshot. Add its parser, metavar, help, and dispatch in `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py`. In `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`, add `bridge-status` to the `_BRIDGE` routing census and update `_dispatch_bridge` so the top-level compatibility alias is routable through the identical `_bridge_commands` argument parser/core. Remove only `bridge-status` from `_RETIRED_BRIDGE_COMMANDS` in `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py`; keep `purge-bridge` retired. The compatibility alias is routable but intentionally hidden from top-level help, while canonical `bridge status` is documented. Regenerate the byte-exact `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt` golden so its command list includes `status`; then regenerate `docs/cli-reference.md` with `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` and pass its `--check` drift gate. The hidden alias routes through `_BRIDGE` rather than the intercept ladder, so it must remain absent from generated top-level help and does not enter `INTERCEPT_COMMANDS`. Update the retired-command absence scan and add canonical/legacy parity coverage.

Status never calls `steal()` and never sleeps for a lease. It reads the authoritative last-pass ref, optional matching rich detail, pause state, and lock ref OID/fence/lease metadata.

Text and structured output expose the same verdict and facts. Co-occurring conditions resolve by total precedence `PAUSED > RUNNING > FOREIGN > FAILED > STALE > HEALTHY`; `NEVER_RUN` applies only when neither a durable record nor a live lock exists. The dominant verdict determines the exit code, while lower-precedence facts remain in structured output for diagnosis. Exact verdict and exit contract:

- `HEALTHY`, matching successful last-pass record, exit 0.
- `PAUSED`, matching state while intentionally paused, exit 0 even when old; pause takes precedence over age failure.
- `RUNNING`, lock currently held in this single snapshot, exit 0 and include lock OID, fence, and lease.
- `STALE`, matching non-paused record older than an explicitly supplied `--max-age`, exit 1.
- Omitting `--max-age` disables age failure; there is no implicit threshold.
- `FOREIGN`, durable record environment differs from the explicitly selected target, exit 1 with both ids.
- `NEVER_RUN`, no durable last-pass record and no live lock, exit 1. The compatibility spelling preserves the former missing-status failure class and exit 1 while using the new shared schema and message.
- `FAILED`, last-pass records a process-surviving hard failure, exit 1 with `failure_kind`.
- `CRASHED` is not inferred by one status invocation. It is the canary result when two read-only snapshots separated by the lock blobs observed `lease_secs` show the same lock OID and fence; exit 1 in the canary and escalation path.

The lock blob is the lease configuration source. The holder carries `lease_secs`; current acquisition defaults to `_ref_lock.DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS=120` when no configured override exists. The canary waits the first snapshots observed holder lease, not a separate wall-clock threshold. Because the workflow job has a fixed 10-minute timeout, an observed `lease_secs` above 480 seconds is rejected immediately as a clear operational failure with exit 1 and the existing escalation path; the canary never caps the wait and misclassifies a still-live lock. The default 120-second lease remains within budget.

The two witnesses are deliberately separate. Last-pass records success and failures for which the process can execute finalization. SIGKILL, OOM, or runner teardown cannot update last-pass; only a non-advancing lock fence across one lease witnesses that crash. The scheduled canary takes two status snapshots separated by the observed lease and classifies advancing fence as `RUNNING` and unchanged OID/fence as `CRASHED`. It does not compare wall-clock heartbeat timestamps.

## Canary cutover and rollback

Roll out producer before consumer: retain explicit `REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE=github-api` during bootstrap until the reconciler producer has successfully written `refs/reconciler/last-pass` at least once, preventing a false `NEVER_RUN` alert; only then switch/default production to canonical `bridge status`. The canary workflow first fetches `+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*`, explicitly targets environment `reconciler`, takes two snapshots when a lock is present, and keeps existing ticket escalation, dedup tags, and failure behavior. The canonical source performs no GitHub Actions heartbeat API query.

For one release, retain the GitHub Actions API heartbeat source behind explicit rollback selection `REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE=github-api`; default is `status`. Tests cover both selections. Removing that rollback option is out of scope and will be separately tracked after the compatibility window.

## Architecture record and numbering convention

Create ADR `0094-reconciler-last-pass-two-witness-status.md` explaining the authoritative last-pass ref, fixed rich-detail file, write-before-release ordering, separate stalled-fence crash witness, rejected timestamp and accumulating-file alternatives, and rollback. Its `Relation to ADR 0031` section explicitly identifies ADR 0031s live fence progress witness, lease-carried-in-blob expiry rule, and single CAS/mismatch classifier as the established pattern being extended; ADR 0094 adds only the authoritative last-pass witness and canary consumption. Allocate it through the collision-proof convention: generate `docs/adr/.numbers/0094` whose content is the ADR filename, regenerate the derived `docs/adr/README.md` with `scripts/gen_adr_index.py`, and pass both `scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` and `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`. If an update from `origin/main` claims 0094 before push, use the next free four-digit number, regenerate marker/index, and update references rather than resolving by sharing a number.

## Verification plan

Author all behavioral tests RED-first under held-out TDD. The happy path proves a matching durable success. Held-out edge and E2E tests prove:

- canonical and legacy command parity for options, text/JSON, schema, errors, exits, hidden legacy help, and no mutation;
- `HEALTHY`, `PAUSED`, `RUNNING`, `STALE`, `FOREIGN`, `NEVER_RUN`, `FAILED`, and canary `CRASHED` contracts;
- omitted `--max-age` disables age failure and paused remains exit 0;
- local last-pass identity cannot masquerade as `reconciler`, while inbound legacy Jira identity and workflow default remain unchanged;
- hard process-surviving failure pushes minimal durable state before lock release even when workflow commit-back is skipped;
- SIGKILL/OOM is represented only by stalled fence and two-snapshot lease classification;
- last-pass CAS contention follows the exact three-attempt backoff and persistent ref push failure fails loudly without leaving the lock held;
- fixed rich detail mismatch/missing behavior and absence of unbounded per-pass files;
- a real-ref held-out E2E has the canary fetch and read actual `refs/reconciler/*`, covering advancing and stalled live lock-fence snapshots without mocking status output;
- canary consumes canonical status, preserves ticket escalation, defaults away from heartbeat API queries only after the producer bootstrap write, and supports explicit GitHub API rollback;
- all old bridge preview/sync/pause/resume consumers and behavior remain green;
- post-change semantic plus `rg` sweeps prove removed producer and baseline symbols have no live references;
- ADR marker bijection and generated index are current.

Proving commands are the focused status, reconciler health, lock, canary, workflow-wiring, help, and compatibility suites, ADR checker commands, then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` from the worktree virtualenv.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] New `bridge status` and hidden re-introduced `bridge-status` are identical read-only entrypoints while preview/sync/pause/resume remain compatible and purge-bridge remains retired.
- [x] Exact structured verdict and exit contracts above are implemented, including never-run, foreign, omitted max-age, paused, hard failure, and held lock.
- [x] Local last-pass and CI identities cannot collide while inbound legacy Jira identity and the workflow default `reconciler` remain unchanged.
- [x] One consolidated producer records success and process-surviving failure before lock release with exact CAS retry and loud persistent-push failure.
- [x] Legacy producer and baseline symbols are absent after all consumers are updated, proven by semantic and string-reference sweeps.
- [x] Rich detail uses one fixed rolling file and safely degrades when missing or mismatched.
- [x] Crash detection uses two read-only fence snapshots across the observed holder lease; status never mutates or blocks for a lease.
- [x] Canary ref fetch, status default, ticket escalation, no canonical heartbeat API query, and one-release rollback source are proven.
- [x] ADR number marker bijection and generated index follow the current convention and both ADR checker commands pass.
- [x] [operator-attested] RED-first focused tests plus full lint, typecheck, and test gates prove contracts and compatibility.
